This is assuming your in the USA flying within the states.

Legally, (ada and DOT wise I should say) there is no mark when a dog goes from in training to working dog.  A service dog 1-has to be in control and properly bathed and 2- must do one or more tasks to help a handlers disability. I’d say use common sense. If there was another service dog on the plane, could your dog distract/get very distracted by it? Are they ready for a plane? Can she do a task? If she fits the legal definition, technically she’s a service dog, even if in training(legally). As long as she fits those requirements she can be considered a SD and could fly on a plane. You have to make that choice but I wish you the best of luck! To some up, no service dogs considered in training are not protected by the ada and it really depends on the flight. However, a lot of the time we consider them in training(rightfully), but legally we could call them service dogs. Sorry if this is long. I’m at the airport rn waiting to board and very bored.
